highest_value_security_question.hypothesis: Backing-file path/device/inode identity plus stable backing-file hash is sufficient to prove the SQLite code bytes actually resident in the observed process.
highest_value_security_question.strongest_counterhypothesis: A MAP_PRIVATE/COW process mapping can diverge in resident bytes while path/device/inode and backing-file hash remain unchanged, so file-identity attestation alone cannot prove process-memory byte identity.

local_discriminator.interpretation: The counterworld survives the backing-file identity primitives. This is not an exact repository import test and not target-VPS evidence.

go_oob_experiment.reason: The current attestor explicitly claims mapped backing-object identity for one observed process generation, not full process-memory byte integrity.

architecture_delta.delta: Before any final release claim equates mapped SQLite backing-object identity with actual executed in-memory code identity, either add a measured process-memory/tamper boundary or keep the higher-level receipt explicitly scoped to backing-object identity.
architecture_delta.strongest_counterargument: Private COW modification requires a write-capable in-process or process-tampering capability and may be outside the intended threat model; adding memory-byte attestation could add complexity without protecting a declared trust boundary.
architecture_delta.next_falsifier: On the accepted target lane, test the real Frank service against a controlled private-page/code-tamper attempt and measure whether the actual service hardening prevents the intervention or whether a stronger executable-memory integrity receipt is needed.
architecture_delta.rollback: Do not merge the experiment branch or change release semantics unless an exact target test demonstrates material relevance.
